plan: This is structurally a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my exit point in the ascending clock, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (the price where the last competitor exits), not my own bid. Bidding my true value ($30) is the dominant strategy—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. I'll bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit.

Since the auction mechanism functions like a second-price auction (the clock ends when only one bidder remains, and the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value of $28 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > competitors' bids) and never overpay, since the price I'd pay is determined by others' bids, not my own. This maximizes expected profit.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit price in an ascending clock auction with 2 other bidders (effectively second-price mechanics), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. Bidding exactly $22 ensures I win whenever the clock price would leave me profit (price < value) and I never pay more than my value.
